Institute For Youth Development Finds Youth At Risk
Of Being "Snared By A 'Web' Of  5 Linked Risk Factors"

SOURCE: Institute for Youth Development

IYD Releases America’s Youth: Measuring the Risk; Most Young People Succeeding in Face of Five Related Risk Factors
(Ed. note: Is muddled thinking a risk factor? This study lumps marijuana in with "drugs." It speaks of "the great degree of interconnection between risk factors," but it would also seem that there are certain behaviors in 14-15 year-olds that really correlate to poor parental supervision as much as they correlate to one another.)

WASHINGTON, March 23, 1998

PRNewswire
The Institute for Youth Development (IYD) has released America’s Youth: Measuring the Risk, 2nd edition, a comprehensive review of data showing that, while young people are at risk of being snared by a "web" of five, inextricably linked risk factors, most are successfully navigating adolescence.

The five major risk factors facing youth today—alcohol, drugs, sex, tobacco, and violence—are interconnected, the report concludes. For example, youth ages 12-17 who smoke are 8 times more likely to use illicit drugs and 11 times more likely to drink heavily than nonsmoking youths. And 87% of 14-15 year-olds who are regular users of marijuana have had sexual intercourse.

At the same time, America’s Youth: Measuring the Risk shows that, despite these risks, most youngsters are faring well. For example:

"We must celebrate those youth who are succeeding, but at the same time we must recognize that the risks facing them are serious, each potentially leading to greater dangers," commented IYD founder and president Shepherd Smith. "It is the great degree of interconnection between risk factors that convinced us to move beyond our work at Americans for a Sound AIDS/HIV Policy—for which we are largely known—and to take a broader approach to the problems facing youth by creating the Institute for Youth Development."

IYD is a non-partisan, non-profit organization that promotes a consistent, comprehensive risk-avoidance message to youth for five harmful risk-behaviors that are inextricably linked: alcohol, drugs, sex, tobacco, and violence. IYD believes that reaching our children with sound messages at vulnerable ages can spare them personal tragedies, and help them enjoy happier and healthier lives.

SOURCE: Institute for Youth Development
